extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer-review researchers, and those developing/implementing instruments to evaluate peer-review quality
extracted.subtask_description: Development, implementation, and validation of a five-point holistic scoring rubric (HESR) for editors to evaluate the quality and value of peer reviews, with emphasis on how reviews inform editorial decision-making. Includes rubric content, anchoring, calibration, and psychometric validation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic Editor’s Scoring Rubric (HESR) — overall instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: A five-point global scoring rubric developed for editors to assess the quality of a peer review with emphasis on the degree to which it informs a holistic appreciation for the submission under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented as a 5-point criterion-referenced scale with anchors at each point; editors score reviews independently and report scores to a third party for blinding. The HESR was iteratively refined after a pilot (first 14 reviews) and used for full implementation. Intended to be practical and simple to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision 1 — Insights on value to readership and alignment with current literature
rubrics_metrics.description: A high-quality review provides insights that reflect both the value to readership and alignment with the current literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as one of the core characteristics that define the anchors for each score point; a 5-rating review should provide these insights comprehensively. Editors reviewed mission/vision statements and reviewer guidelines from major journals to operationalize this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision 2 — Consideration of appropriateness of study methods and relevant scholarship tenets
rubrics_metrics.description: A quality review considers the appropriateness of the study method(s) and relevant tenets of education scholarship (i.e., methodological critique and conceptual rigor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a central axis of the rubric anchors — reviewers should comment on study design, methods, and alignment with accepted methodological standards for the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision 3 — Mentoring feedback to improve manuscript and reviewer skillset
rubrics_metrics.description: A quality review provides feedback that offers mentorship to authors on how to improve their manuscript as well as guidance that could improve the reviewer’s own skill set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive, actionable, educative feedback is required for higher anchor levels; providing specific suggestions for improvement and mentoring language is part of scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree to which the review informs the final evaluation (standalone utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rubric anchors incorporate the degree to which the review informs the final evaluation of the submission — a top-rated review could serve as the final evaluation (a 'Gold standard review').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rating of 5 denotes a review that provides all three provisions and could stand alone as the manuscript’s final evaluation; this criterion ties reviewer quality to editorial decision utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-point anchor descriptors (adjective labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each numeric point on the HESR is labeled with adjectives to characterize performance: 5-Excellent, 4-Very good, 3-Good, 2-Below average, 1-Unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjective descriptors were added after a preliminary calibration exercise to improve clarity. Anchors are criterion-referenced and intended to reduce leniency bias and guide consistent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicality and simplicity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation system should be practical and simple to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literature and prior work informed the need for a tool that editors will feasibly adopt during editorial workflows; complexity should be minimized to encourage use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion-referenced orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: The scoring system should be criterion referenced rather than purely norm-referenced or subjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchors describe behavioral/qualitative features of reviews at each level rather than relying only on endpoint labels; this supports more valid, actionable scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to capture differences in expert reviewers' perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The rubric should be able to capture differences in expert reviewers’ perspectives and legitimate divergent opinions about what constitutes good scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design acknowledges that expert reviewers may legitimately disagree; rubric should allow nuanced and varying scores that reflect those perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rater training is necessary to ensure proper implementation of the rubric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior work suggests rater training improves reliability; the authors note editors had regular discussions and performed a preliminary calibration exercise to refine clarity and scoring consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-full-scale / distribution requirement (reduce leniency bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: A valid editorial scoring mechanism should reflect the variability of peer-review quality by using the full range of the evaluation scale (i.e., avoid skewing to high scores / leniency bias).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the a priori validity assumptions: HESR scores should have a distribution where all rating options are used. Observed skew in prior semantic-differential scoring motivated criterion-referenced anchors and calibration to increase use of lower ratings where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of relative consistency over absolute inter-rater agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Because editorial perspectives vary, the rubric aims for relative consistency (e.g., high ICC, strong correlations) across editors rather than perfect absolute identical ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors argued that absolute agreement may be low-to-moderate while relative consistency (rank-ordering and correlation) is more achievable and meaningful for editorial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation metric — percent absolute and close agreement (+1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure agreement between editors using percentage of identical ratings (absolute agreement) and percentage within one point (+1) as indicators of absolute and near agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside correlation and ICC to characterize inter-rater concordance; in the study absolute agreement was 37.8% and ~47.8% were within one point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation metric — Spearman rho correlation for ordinal data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Spearman rho to assess the strength of the relationship between ratings across raters for ordinal-level rubric data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied interpretation guidance from Schober et al. (ranges for negligible to very strong correlations); used to complement ICC and percent agreement (study found rho ≈ 0.703).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation metric — Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) model and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute an ICC (one-way random effects, average measures, absolute agreement) to assess relative consistency of ratings across editors, interpreted using Cicchetti’s criteria (e.g., ICC < .4 poor, .40–.59 fair, .60–.74 good, .75–1.0 excellent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors selected ICC model assumptions: associate editors treated as random, senior editor fixed, design not fully crossed, focus on average measures. ICC in study was 0.795 (interpreted as excellent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation metric — association with editorial decision (implication / predictive validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher HESR ratings should be associated with greater likelihood that the reviewer’s recommendation agrees with the manuscript’s final editorial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test via chi-square association (categorize averaged ratings into bins e.g., 1–1.5, 2–2.5, etc.) and logistic regression predicting reviewer/editor agreement; report effect sizes (e.g., Cramer’s phi) and odds ratios to demonstrate practical implication. In the study, higher ratings correlated with greater agreement and senior editor ratings predicted match (Exp[B] reported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding and data handling procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize bias, editors reported their HESR scores to a third party who maintained a secured database linking ratings for blinded analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blinding the score submission process prevents recall and identity biases; third-party management was used during the pilot and implementation phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration / iterative refinement procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a preliminary calibration exercise (pilot) to compare scorings, identify clarity issues, revise rubric wording and add adjective descriptors by consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors paused after first 14 reviews to revise the rubric based on discrepancies, improving clarity and providing anchors that aided subsequent implementation.
